text: Kestrelline Rail will build its new maintenance depot in Lowen Ridge, company and city officials said Thursday at a short briefing outside the municipal transport office. I was told the site will go on a vacant freight parcel near Alder Spur, where survey crews were marking boundaries by midmorning. Transport manager Elia Voss said the depot should open by late next year and bring about 80 jobs, including mechanics, dispatchers and cleaners. Mayor Teren Hale called the project “a practical fit” for the city’s rail corridor. Workers I saw on site were unloading fencing and setting up temporary power, while residents nearby said they had been told construction would begin in March.
